bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar prioritises affordable medical education in proposed PPP medical colleges
bihar_raw_news.content: Government Policies 1 min read Bihar prioritises affordable medical education in proposed PPP medical colleges Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said Bihar-based investors and doctors would get preference in brownfield medical college projects, with the government seeking to expand capacity while protecting public interest and patient rights. Madan Kumar & madan.kumar TOI.in Published On Oct 17, 2026 at 06:49 PM IST Select ETEducation as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Affordable medical education, quality healthcare govt’s priorities: Samrat Patna: CM Samrat Choudhary said the Bihar govt’s foremost priority is to ensure quality healthcare in medical colleges while keeping medical education affordable for students, as he chaired a review meeting of the health department. Choudhary said the govt was working to expand medical education across Bihar while protecting students’ interests, upholding patients’ rights and improving access to reliable, affordable and high-quality health services. He said proposals under the public-private partnership model must be guided by public interest and should strengthen the state’s health system without compromising govt ownership. Advt The meeting reviewed proposals for establishing and operating brownfield medical colleges under the PPP model. Officials discussed ways to expand the capacity of medical colleges and hospitals by making better use of existing infrastructure and drawing on the expertise and investment capacity of both the public and private sectors. The objective, officials said, is to make healthcare services more accessible, effective and professionally managed. Choudhary said Bihar-based investors should be given preference in the establishment of brownfield medical colleges so that residents of the state receive direct benefits. He also said doctors from Bihar willing to participate in such initiatives should be accorded priority. All stakeholders, he added, must work with the welfare of the people as the central consideration. Health Secretary Kumar Ravi gave a detailed presentation on the proposed framework for operating brownfield medical colleges under the PPP model. He said hospitals would be required to display key information on prescribed charges, patient eligibility, bed categories and patients’ rights in both Hindi and English on hospital premises and online platforms. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Sets 500 MW Rooftop Solar Target for Government Buildings by 2029–30 - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Sets 500 MW Rooftop Solar Target for Government Buildings by 2029–30 17 Oct 2026 1 min read Why in News? The Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA) has set a target of installing 500 MW of rooftop solar capacity on government buildings by 2029–30 . Key Points Implementing Agency: Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA) will oversee the installation of grid-connected rooftop solar power plants on government buildings across Bihar. Target: The initiative aims to achieve 500 MW of rooftop solar capacity by 2029–30 . Associated Campaign: The project is being implemented under Phase 3 of the Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign . Implementation Model: Solar projects will be implemented through the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model . Building Identification: Government departments have been asked to submit lists of buildings under their jurisdiction for assessing their suitability for rooftop solar installations. Power Purchase Agreement: The meeting discussed the draft Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and the roles and responsibilities of BREDA, government departments and solar developers. bihar_raw_news.content: About Us Contact Us अब आप न्यूज्ड हिंदी में पढ़ सकते हैं। यहाँ क्लिक करें Home » Beyond Metros » Bihar Bullet Train Plan: Patna to Varanasi in 50 Minutes? Check Proposed Stations Bihar Bullet Train Plan: Patna to Varanasi in 50 Minutes? Check Proposed Stations Bihar could get bullet train connectivity if the proposed corridor extension moves ahead. The plan may connect Patna with Varanasi in around 50 minutes, but stations remain unconfirmed for now. By Newsd Published on : Sat 17th October 2026, 02:28 PM Follow Newsd On Bihar Bullet Train Plan: Bihar may get a bullet train connection if plans to extend the Delhi -Varanasi corridor to Patna and Siliguri move ahead. The proposed route could connect several cities in Bihar and make travel to Delhi and Uttar Pradesh much faster. the plan hasn’t been approved fully yet. The station locations and construction dates are also not confirmed, so it’s still a proposal for now. Patna to Varanasi in Around 50 Minutes The proposed plan could cut the travel time between Patna and Varanasi to around 50 minutes. This would make the journey much faster than regular trains. But the actual travel time will depend on the final route, station locations and train speed. Bihar Traffic Rules Crackdown: ₹15.5 Crore in Fines, What Motorists Need to Know Faster travel could help people who travel between Bihar and Uttar Pradesh for work, business, education or tourism. If Patna gets connected to the wider bullet train network, passengers could also have a faster travel option towards Delhi. The reported Delhi-Varanasi journey time is around three hours and 50 minutes. The travel time between Delhi and Patna hasn’t been confirmed because the proposed extension’s route and operating details are still undecided. Which Bihar Cities Can Get Bullet Train Stations? Several cities have been mentioned as possible stops if the high-speed rail network is extended through Bihar. The proposed stations include: Buxar Ara Patna Begusarai Khagaria Katihar The route could connect western, central and eastern parts of Bihar. It may also continue towards Siliguri in West Bengal. The final station list hasn’t been confirmed yet. Route, Cost and Project Updates The proposed Delhi-Varanasi corridor has been reported to cover around 865 kilometres, with an estimated cost of Rs 1.21 lakh crore. The Union Budget 2026-27 also announced the Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri high-speed rail corridors. The government has said the latter will connect important cities in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal. Samrat Choudhary Cabinet Approves 5 Airports and 9 Heliports in Bihar, Free Pickup-Drop Planned Other cities mentioned along the proposed routes include Mathura, Agra, Firozabad, Etawah, Kannauj, Lucknow, Rae Bareli, Prayagraj and Bhadohi. A separate link of around 135 kilometres between Lucknow and Ayodhya has also been discussed. Ground and aerial LiDAR surveys have reportedly been carried out for the corridor. Technical studies, route planning, government approvals and land acquisition will be important steps before construction can move ahead. The detailed plans and timelines will depend on further decisions. Related

national_raw_news.title: Space Minister Dr Jitendra Singh says, India’s space economy is likely to reach 40-45 billion US ...
national_raw_news.content: Minister of State for Atomic Energy and Space Dr Jitendra Singh has said that India’s Space economy, currently valued at around 9 billion, is expected to reach 40 to 45 billion dollars over the next seven to eight years. He said this during a media Roundtable on Space, Sovereignty and New Economy organised by Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. He stressed that greater domestic and international investment, faster regulatory approvals and sustainable business models would be essential to scaling up Indian enterprises and expanding their presence in global markets. The minister said the opening of India’s Space sector had produced significant results within just five to six years. He said that India’s experience demonstrates the potential of bringing government institutions and private industry together in a sector that requires substantial technological expertise, investment and long-term commitment. The priority now, he said, is to convert these capabilities into commercially viable businesses with the scale to compete internationally. The Minister also stressed the need for timely regulatory approvals, lower business costs and stronger supply-chain integration. He said that India must now move beyond demonstrating its technological capabilities to building globally competitive commercial space companies. Dr Jitendra Singh stressed that generating demand is essential for the growth of private space companies. On investment and international cooperation, the Minister said, India is opening up opportunities for capital and partnerships while continuing to strengthen indigenous capabilities. He said greater investment can support technology development, manufacturing and access to international markets, while domestic capabilities remain important for national security and strategic autonomy. Dr Singh said the opening of the space sector to private participation reflects the value of enabling new players to contribute alongside established public institutions.

national_raw_news.content: The High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), constituted by the Supreme Court to enquire into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and at places outside Delhi, during the month of July this year, has launched a portal for submitting complaints and representations. The portal http://hpec.nic.in has been launched for the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel. The Ministry of Home Affairs said that the HPEC shall examine all issues enumerated in Supreme Court’s Order. The Ministry added that priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side. The Ministry said that the Portal is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons. The affected persons and other stakeholders are encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints/representations, making use of the formats as applicable. Those who wish to submit the complaints, representations and other relevant material physically can do so at the Office of the HPEC at Shiksha Sadan, New Delhi between 2 PM and 4 PM on all working days. Submissions can also be sent by post at the above address or by email at hpec 2026.enquiry [at] nic [dot] in. The Ministry also said that any person who wants to provide information or suggestions relating to the issues referred to the HPEC may also do so through the portal.

national_raw_news.title: Centre seeks reports from Punjab govt over killings of anti-drug activists amid narcotics-linked ...
national_raw_news.content: Former Punjab BJP president Sunil Jakhar has written to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, seeking investigations by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) into alleged drug operations being run from prisons in Punjab. Mr Jakhar also demanded a probe by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) into the black money linked to the drug trade in the state. In the letter, Mr Jakhar, while referring to the recent murder of anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota in Mansa, said that a drug inspector who had served in the same district was arrested two years ago. He mentioned that the DGP had claimed that the said inspector was the kingpin of a gang linked to imprisoned drug traffickers. The network had links to cross-border drug trafficking. Substantial assets worth crores of rupees belonging to him were uncovered. Mr Jakhar said that instead of initiating an NIA investigation or referring the case to the ED, the said drug inspector was reinstated by the Aam Aadmi Party government after his bail. He said that the drug inspector was also appointed to an important position at his department’s headquarters. Mr Jakhar has called for action against what he described as a drug trade operating from prisons, allegedly under state government patronage and for the exposure of the money laundering linked to it.

national_raw_news.title: India’s Space Economy Poised to Reach USD 40–45 Billion in 7–8 Years: Jitendra Singh
national_raw_news.content: India’s space economy, currently valued at around USD 9 billion, is projected to grow to USD 40–45 billion over the next seven to eight years, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology and Space Jitendra Singh said, highlighting the growing role of private investment and commercial participation in the sector. Speaking at a media roundtable on “Space, Sovereignty and New Economy”, organised by the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Singh said India must move beyond demonstrating technological capabilities and focus on developing globally competitive commercial space enterprises. He emphasised that increased domestic and foreign investment, predictable demand, faster regulatory approvals and sustainable business models would be essential to expanding India’s presence in the global space market. The roundtable brought together representatives from the space industry, entrepreneurship, academia and the international space community to discuss private investment, commercial opportunities, supply-chain development and national security considerations. Among the participants were Vinod Kumar, Director (Promotion) at the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), and Aisha Bowe, founder and CEO of STEMBoard and LINGO, former NASA engineer and Blue Origin astronaut. Singh said the opening of India’s space sector to private participation in 2019–2020 under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership had delivered significant results within five to six years. He said collaboration between government institutions and private companies had helped create new opportunities in a sector requiring advanced technology, substantial investment and long-term commitment. The next priority, he added, was to translate these technological capabilities into commercially viable businesses capable of competing internationally. Highlighting the importance of market demand, Singh said government agencies could play a crucial role as anchor customers for emerging space enterprises. He said the government’s use-case-based approach, including support for proof-of-concept projects, could help private companies demonstrate their technologies and move towards commercial deployment. A predictable customer base, he noted, would encourage companies to invest in manufacturing, develop market-ready products and establish sustainable revenue streams. The Minister also called for faster regulatory approvals, reduced business costs and stronger integration of domestic companies into global supply chains. He said businesses seeking installation or export licences should receive approvals within clearly defined timelines to improve operational efficiency and investor confidence. Referring to Goods and Services Tax (GST)-related measures for space products, Singh stressed that regulatory reforms must deliver tangible benefits to the industry. He said sustainable investment depended on predictable demand, efficient administrative processes and clear opportunities for commercial growth. On international cooperation, Singh said India was expanding opportunities for foreign investment and partnerships while continuing to strengthen indigenous technological capabilities. Greater investment, he said, could support research, manufacturing and access to international markets, while domestic capabilities remained essential for national security and strategic autonomy. He advocated closer collaboration between government institutions and private enterprises, supported by international partnerships, to help Indian companies expand their customer base and participate in global supply chains. The Minister also highlighted the growing use of space technology in sectors beyond satellite launches and exploration. He said satellite communications, geospatial applications and Earth observation technologies were increasingly supporting infrastructure development, agriculture, disaster management, defence and the monitoring of government projects. Singh cited the use of space-based technologies for project clearances, tracking implementation timelines and geotagging development works. India was also providing space-based information and disaster management support to neighbouring countries, including Myanmar, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, he said. These applications, according to the Minister, demonstrated the potential of space technology to improve public services, support development and generate commercial opportunities. He said the broader economic value of the space sector would increasingly come from downstream services, satellite data applications and technology-driven solutions, alongside launch vehicles and satellite manufacturing. Emphasising the need to balance national capabilities with global cooperation, Singh said India should continue developing indigenous technologies while working with international partners to attract investment and expand market access. He also called for flexible policies and openness to new ideas as technologies and industry requirements evolve. The Minister said India’s next phase of space-sector growth would depend on converting technological achievements into commercially successful enterprises through greater investment, stronger public-private partnerships, predictable demand and efficient regulatory processes.
